description: Run the deterministic preflight on an intent spec before handing it to an implementation agent. Six calibrated checks — title, objective, outcomes, constraints, edge cases, verification — computed by pure functions: no model call, no network, the same spec always gets the same verdict. Pass a spec inline to check before saving, pass intentId to check a specific saved intent, pass repoRoot to check the intent.md of the repository you are working in, or pass nothing to resolve the repo-bound intent.md from MCP workspace roots or the launch directory. The repo-bound intent.md is the one at the repository root or, when there is none, the single intent.md in an intent/ folder (intent/intent.md or intent/<feature>/intent.md), where Anthropic's AI-native SDLC playbook keeps it. Pass path to choose among several, or to check a file with another name. When the repository has no intent.md, or cannot be identified, it refuses rather than grading an unrelated intent; pass repoRoot to name the repository, or intentId to check a specific saved intent. A failing verdict names the exact blockers; repair the fields and re-run. This is the gate that runs at preflight.pathmode.io.

intentId.description: Check a specific saved intent by id. Ignored when spec is passed.

path.description: The intent file to check, when the repository keeps several in intent/ or names it something other than intent.md, e.g. intent/checkout/intent.md. Relative to repoRoot when that is passed, otherwise to the repository a no-argument call resolves; an absolute path is used as is. Ignored when spec or intentId is passed.

repoRoot.description: Absolute path of the repository you are working in; Pathmode checks its intent.md, at the root or in its intent/ folder. Pass it when a no-argument call is refused because your MCP client declares no workspace roots, or declares several. Ignored when spec or intentId is passed.

spec.description: Check this spec directly (before saving). When omitted, resolve the repo-bound intent.md from MCP roots or cwd. A repository with no intent.md is refused, not answered with the workspace current intent; pass intentId to choose a saved intent deliberately.

constraints.description: Hard limits the implementation must respect

currentState.description: How this works today, before the change — existing behavior and workarounds, so the implementation knows what must not regress. Omit for net-new capability.

decisions.description: Decisions settled during design + the alternatives ruled out, so the agent does not relitigate them. Omit to keep the existing decisions. Locally a supplied list replaces them ([] clears); connected, supplied decisions are added to the workspace log, which a save never shrinks.

id.description: Existing intent id. Pass it back when re-saving an intent you already saved so the file is updated (version bumped, status preserved) instead of replaced. Omit for a new intent.

implementationContext.description: What the repo actually looks like where this change lands: the files and modules involved, what already exists, what it would touch, how to verify it. You are in the working tree — go read it. Markdown, sub-headings welcome. Advisory: it never changes the readiness verdict, it just stops the implementing agent from rediscovering the codebase.

objective.description: Why this matters — the problem and who has it

outcomes.description: Observable, testable state changes. The structured form may carry an optional provider-neutral saved-query measurement recipe.

resultSelector.description: Optional path into a compound provider response

provider.description: System that owns the saved query, e.g. "posthog"

id.description: Stable id of the query. An id, never a name — names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

kind.description: How to interpret the id, e.g. "saved_insight"

productChoices.description: New open product choices, never human answers. Existing choices are preserved.

productId.description: Which product this intent belongs to (cloud mode only). Omit it and the server resolves it when the workspace has exactly one real product; if it cannot, the save fails with PRODUCT_REQUIRED and the candidate list, and you should ask the user which one and retry with an explicit id rather than guessing — a GitHub binding hangs off the product, so it decides which repository merge verification applies to.

scope.description: Scope boundaries — what to build and what to avoid

inScope.description: What is in scope for this intent

outOfScope.description: What is explicitly out of scope

checks.description: Feedback-loop checks (preferred over the legacy test buckets)

name: check_intent_readiness
title: Check Intent Readiness (Preflight)
